exposure: Mode of subsequent birth (vaginal vs. caesarean section)
cohort: Pregnant women with previous obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI)
finding: There was no significant difference in bowel function or quality of life between women with previous OASI who had a subsequent vaginal birth compared to those who had a caesarean section.
mod_finding: Women with previous OASI who had a subsequent caesarean section had significantly higher odds of having poor 'incontinence impact' and 'physical limitations'.
